newsitem.title: UK: U.K. North Sea operating costs hit bottom - WoodMac.
newsitem.headline: U.K. North Sea operating costs hit bottom - WoodMac.

text.p: North Sea oil and gas field operating costs have sunk to their lowest levels in over ten years but could start to rise again shortly, according to a study published by consultants Wood MacKenzie on Thursday.
"Weighted average operating costs for fields in the U.K. have dropped by 23 percent since 1990 in real terms. Sixty percent of this fall has occurred since the end of 1994," said Wood MacKenzie.

The Edinburgh-based consultants said platform de-manning, rationalisation of operations and other cost-saving initiatives have resulted in the lowest average unit operating cost since the early 1980s.
But the cost of extracting oil from mature fields and development of frontier acres west of the Shetland Islands will counter low cost production from many of the new and smaller field developments.

"From our base case analysis we have forecast the level of unit operating cost to gradually increase over the next five years from 2.64 stg/barrel of oil equivalent (boe) in 1996 to 2.86 stg/boe in 2001 in real terms," WoodMac said.
WoodMac surveyed estimates from 25 companies which account for over 90 percent of all operating expense on the U.K. Continental Shelf.

British Gas was found to have the lowest unit operating cost at 1.89 stg/boe in 1996, while U.S. independent Oryx, which recently acquired mature assets from DuPont's Conoco and Chevron, had the highest cost portfolio at 4.86 stg/boe this year.

The Shell /Exxon joint venture, which represents about 24 percent of total British output, benefited from below average costs of about 2.44 stg/boe, while British Petroleum with 19 percent of oil and gas production came close to the U.K. average of 2.64 stg/boe.
